notes: Fiscal years are assumed to align with calendar-year reporting shown in O’Reilly’s FY2025 and FY2024 earnings materials (year ended Dec 31). ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))
EBIT is proxied by GAAP operating income from the earnings release income statement tables.
D&A is taken as 'Depreciation and amortization of property, equipment and intangibles' from the cash flow statement.
Capex is taken as 'Purchases of property and equipment' from the cash flow statement (reported as an absolute positive in this package).

NWC is computed as (Total current assets - cash and cash equivalents) - Total current liabilities. This produces a persistently negative NWC because current liabilities exceed non-cash current assets in the balance sheet tables; definition includes items such as current operating lease liabilities and income taxes payable included in current liabilities.

Tax rate is modeled as the historical average effective tax rate computed from (Provision for income taxes) / (Income before income taxes) across 2023–2025. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2025/02/05/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024-results/))
WACC and terminal growth are modeling assumptions (not explicitly disclosed by the company in the materials reviewed).

NOLs: only small foreign NOL carryforwards are disclosed in the 2024 annual report; this package uses the tax-effected NOL amount (~$5.8M) and assumes an 0.80 utilization rate due to uncertainty about jurisdictional usability in a simplified DCF. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/898173/000089817325000020/orly-20241231xars.pdf))

Comps: EV/NTM revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA were left null due to limited free availability of those specific NTM EV-based multiples; forward P/E is included where available from the free market-data source used.

catalysts: 2026 performance versus guidance: comparable store sales growth and operating margin landing at/above the top end of guided ranges. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))

Expansion execution (new store openings) and distribution/fulfillment improvements supporting continued parts availability and market-share gains. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))
company_overview: O’Reilly Automotive is a leading specialty retailer of automotive aftermarket parts, tools, supplies, equipment, and accessories in the U.S., serving both DIY and professional service providers. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))

As of Dec 31, 2025, O’Reilly operated 6,585 stores across 48 U.S. states, Puerto Rico, Mexico, and Canada. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))

The model emphasizes parts availability and disciplined operating cost management to support sustained operating margins. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))
current_context: FY2025 revenue was $17.782B (+6% YoY) and operating income was $3.461B (19.5% of sales), with full-year comparable store sales growth of 4.7%. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))

FY2025 cash flow included net cash provided by operating activities of $2.762B and purchases of property and equipment (capex) of $1.169B. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))

FY2026 guidance (from FY2025 release): total revenue of $18.7B–$19.0B and operating income margin of 19.2%–19.7%, alongside effective tax rate guidance of 22.6% and capex of $1.3B–$1.4B. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth assumes continued store expansion and mid-single-digit comparable store sales, fading gradually over the forecast horizon. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))

Operating margin base-case is anchored near recent GAAP operating income margins (~19.5% in 2023–2025), reflecting cost discipline while continuing reinvestment. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2025/02/05/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024-results/))

Reinvestment intensity is modeled using historical capex as a share of sales (~6.35%) and D&A as a share of sales (~2.74%). ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2025/02/05/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024-results/))

Working capital is modeled as persistently negative (supplier/settlement financing effect) using a consistent NWC definition from the balance sheet. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))
key_risks: SG&A and claim/cost inflation (notably health care and casualty claim cost pressure) could compress operating margins versus the base case. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))

Macro-driven demand softness or competitive share loss could slow revenue growth below the modeled fade profile. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2025/02/05/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024-results/))
Working-capital volatility (supplier terms, inventory turns, and payables/receivables dynamics) may deviate from the persistently negative base-case assumption.

valuation_summary: The DCF base-case uses a stable operating margin and reinvestment profile consistent with FY2023–FY2025 actuals, with a conservative terminal growth rate. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))

Terminal value is computed with a Gordon-growth approach and a modeling WACC assumption to reflect equity + debt financing risk for a mature retailer. ([corporate.oreillyauto.com](https://corporate.oreillyauto.com/2026/02/04/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/))

Peer sanity-check relies on forward P/E for major auto parts retailers/distributors; EV/NTM revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA were left null due to limited free availability of NTM EV-based multiples. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/azo/))
